title: Buddy Petit, the stuttering trumpeter, arrested for his contracts
summary: Buddy Petit took deposits on many jobs; at a longshoremen's picnic a cop doubted he was Petit, and when Petit produced a pile of contracts as proof he was taken to jail.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: But I never got to tell you about my earlier days
A little bit on that first tape about --
Well, my early days were fantastic, you know, because every time I look back on it, I think about it -- I think I told you about Buddy Petit and all that.
You mentioned having worked with him.
But you didn't tell me much about him.
Buddy Petit was a strange character.

You know, in New Orleans they didn't have any union musicians for colored people. So they'd take jobs and get a deposit. And Buddy Petit was very popular at that time, and he'd take all the jobs he could to get the deposit to go and drink.

Well, I was a youngster and I didn't -- I got in on the tail end of his career and the beginning of mine. So they had -- every year the longshoremen, they gave a big picnic in a big lake, a big party with all the different unions. And I happened to be working with him at that time, and we were doing good and playing pretty good. I was scuffling like as usual because I didn't know much about it. So there was a cop stationed on the bandstand. So when we had finished a set, the cop asked some of the guys in the band, he says, "Who's Buddy
Petit?" And one boy would say, "The trumpet man right there. That man." So the cop would say, "Oh, that can't be Buddy Petit." He says, "Don't tell me that can't be Buddy Petit. That's Buddy Petit."

So we finished the next set and he's getting ready to go off the stand and the cop stopped him and says, "Somebody said you're Buddy Petit." He said -- he stuttered, incidentally, you know -- he said, "Th-th-th-th-th-that's me. I'm Buddy Petit. There's only, only one." The cop says, "Oh, c'mon, man, you're not Buddy Petit." He says, "Don-don-don-don't tell me I'm not Buddy Petit," and he reached in his inside coat pocket and pulled out a gang of contracts with his name, you know, and he said, "W-w-w-w-w-what that say there, huh? Don't that say B-b-b-b-b-Buddy Petit?" The cop says, "It does say Buddy Petit. Well, come with me," and took him to jail.

So they had sued him for all the contracts that a lot of people had sued him and he hadn't showed up, and he would send some -- any band, anybody he could find -- on that job, and the people wanted -- well, his name was so big he drew a lot of people, you know, like especially if they gave a dance or whatever it was. So we played without our trumpet all the rest of the night and that was awful.
So it went on like that.
